This was a buy-and-sell experience with four recorded fills, ending with $86 of profit on $1,000 invested. The account dipped to $988 during the run before recovering to finish at $1,086, so the strategy involved a modest setback along the way.

The tradeoff was clear: it gained 8.6% but lagged simply holding SPY, which returned 16.9% over the same window. That is an 8.3 percentage-point gap in exchange for the strategy’s measured 4.8% largest investment decline.

From September 10, 2025 to September 9, 2026, this was not a simple buy-and-hold experience. The RSI-threshold strategy bought and sold SPY 4 times as its signal changed, while keeping the same $1,000 invested throughout the test. The portfolio grew to $1,086, an 8.6% total return.

The ride was uneven. The portfolio’s worst decline began on December 5, 2025 and lasted until March 30, 2026. From its prior high, it fell 4.8%, or $50. That period matched a broader market correction. The S&P 500 reached a record in late December amid expectations for interest-rate cuts, according to [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/sp-500-hits-intraday-record-high-fueled-by-rate-cut-bets-2025-12-24/). By February, investors were also weighing worries about the cost and disruption of artificial intelligence, renewed tariff uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions, [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/business/us-stock-futures-falter-ai-jitters-nasdaq-braces-steep-monthly-fall-2026-02-27/). In late March, rising oil prices and uncertainty around the Iran conflict added further pressure, with the S&P 500 falling 1.7% on March 26 and reaching a new low for the year on March 30, according to [AP](https://apnews.com/article/wall-street-stocks-dow-nasdaq-9f0c2281f1de0bb4abe66bd568598aa5) and [AP](https://apnews.com/article/wall-street-stocks-dow-nasdaq-800109b3445f87f30865196e08363576).

The recovery was quick after that low. The portfolio reached its highest recorded value on April 14, 2026, when stocks rebounded as oil prices eased and investors returned to technology shares, [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-global-markets-2026-04-14/). Those events provide context for the swings, but the test’s result comes from how the RSI rules moved in and out of SPY during the period.

The meaningful tradeoff was performance. Because the benchmark was SPY itself, the comparison was against simply staying invested in the same asset. The strategy earned 8.6%, while the benchmark earned 16.9%, leaving the strategy behind by 8.3 percentage points. In exchange for its active buying and selling, it experienced a measured 4.8% worst drop, but the test shows that it gave up a substantial amount of the benchmark’s return.

frames.text: Buying DOCN once and holding it through this historical run turned $1,000 invested into $4,963, beating SPY’s comparable result of 69.0% with a 396.3% return. The tradeoff was a rough ride: the account later fell $784 from its drawdown peak before recovering, so the strong outcome came with substantial declines along the way.

This was a simple buy-and-hold experience: one purchase of DOCN, followed by staying invested through the whole window from September 1, 2023 to September 9, 2026. The $1,000 starting investment ended at $4,963. There were no additional deposits, so the increase came from the investment rather than new money being added.

The path was very uneven. The portfolio reached $1,747 before its biggest setback began on February 18, 2025. It then fell to $963 by August 1, a $784 decline, or 44.9% from the earlier high. In other words, the position temporarily dropped below the original $1,000 starting amount before recovering. That recovery eventually carried the portfolio to its highest recorded value of $6,784 on June 15, 2026, before it finished the test below that high at $4,963.

DOCN's business results help explain both sides of the journey. DigitalOcean reported continued revenue growth and strong profitability in its 2024 results, but its 2025 outlook called for growth in the low-to-mid teens. That combination could support the business while still leaving the stock vulnerable to high expectations. The company's [2024 results and 2025 guidance](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2024-Financial-Results/default.aspx) provide the underlying evidence. Around the February decline, broader market weakness also pressured cloud and technology shares, while coverage described investor disappointment with the outlook and earlier results as additional reasons for DOCN's weakness [in this market report](https://markets.financialcontent.com/pennwell.bioopticsworld/article/stockstory-2025-2-24-why-digitalocean-docn-stock-is-falling-today). These sources support the explanation, but they do not establish that any single event caused the entire drawdown.

The later recovery is consistent with improving operating momentum. DigitalOcean reported growth in the first quarter of 2025, and in August it reported further growth while raising its full-year revenue guidance [in its Q1 release](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-First-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) and [Q2 release](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2025/DigitalOcean-Announces-Second-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx). By 2026, the company was also highlighting rapidly growing AI-related customer revenue, which helps explain why investors placed more value on its cloud growth story [in the company's Q2 2026 update](https://investors.digitalocean.com/news/news-details/2026/DigitalOcean-Announces-Second-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx). That is an explanation of the recovery's context, not a claim that these announcements alone determined the portfolio value.

Compared with SPY, the tradeoff was unusually large. DOCN returned 396.3% versus 69.0% for the benchmark, a difference of 327.3 percentage points. The extra return came with a much rougher ride: the test recorded a nearly 45% drop from a prior high, including a period when the portfolio was worth less than the original investment. Staying invested therefore produced a far better historical result than the benchmark in this test, but only by accepting a sharp and prolonged decline along the way.

frames.text: Comprar DOCN una vez y mantener la posición terminó muy por encima de SPY en esta experiencia histórica: el resultado fue 396.3%, frente a 69.0% para el referente. La ganancia registrada fue de $3,963 sobre $1,000 invertidos, pero el recorrido fue áspero: en el peor tramo, la cuenta cayó 44.9% desde un máximo anterior antes de recuperarse. El intercambio fue claro: más crecimiento en este periodo, a cambio de soportar caídas mucho más fuertes.

Here's the deeper read on the completed run.

**Setup.** DOCN Comprar y Mantener tested DOCN over 1 de septiembre de 2023 al 9 de septiembre de 2026 using the stored backtest configuration. Entry rule: buy at the start of the period; exit rule: hold through the end.

**How to read it.** **Total return:** +396.3%. The comparison benchmark was SPY at +69.0%. Superó por 327.3 puntos porcentuales versus the benchmark. This is a comparison of historical returns, not an explanation of why the move happened.

**Risk and assumptions.** Max drawdown was -44.9%, the largest peak-to-trough decline captured by the simulation. The run used Solo largo; Peso igual; Sin comisiones/deslizamiento; Referencia: SPY.

Use this as historical simulation evidence, not a prediction or trading recommendation.

La estrategia compró y vendió SPY en dos ocasiones, y terminó con una ganancia de $86 sobre los $1,000 invertidos. El recorrido tuvo una caída máxima de 4.8%, antes de cerrar en $1,086.

El costo de esa experiencia fue quedar por debajo de comprar y mantener el benchmark: rindió 8.6% frente a 16.9%, una diferencia de 8.3 pp. En este periodo, operar con señales ofreció un resultado positivo, pero sacrificó parte del avance del benchmark.

Entre el 10 de septiembre de 2025 y el 9 de septiembre de 2026, la estrategia empezó con $1,000 y terminó con $1,086. No hubo depósitos adicionales, así que el aumento de $86 provino de la inversión. No fue una experiencia de comprar SPY una sola vez y mantenerlo sin cambios: la estrategia realizó 4 compras y ventas.

El recorrido tuvo un tramo difícil. Después de alcanzar $1,039, el valor bajó hasta $988 entre el 5 de diciembre de 2025 y el 30 de marzo de 2026. Eso representa una pérdida registrada de $50 desde ese máximo anterior. Después se recuperó y llegó a su valor más alto, $1,086, el 14 de abril de 2026, nivel con el que terminó el período.

El entorno ayuda a entender por qué hubo tanta variación. En marzo, las noticias sobre el conflicto entre Estados Unidos e Irán impulsaron el precio del petróleo y aumentaron los temores de inflación, mientras la Reserva Federal mantuvo las tasas sin cambios y señaló incertidumbre económica ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/fed-leaves-rates-unchanged-iran-war-shocks-policy-debate-2026-03-18/)). Reuters también reportó que el S&P 500 llegó a caer cerca de 9% tras el inicio del conflicto, antes de recuperarse con expectativas de una desescalada y ganancias corporativas sólidas ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/sp-500-hits-first-intraday-record-high-since-us-iran-war-2026-04-15/)). Esos hechos ofrecen contexto para el retroceso y la recuperación observados, pero no demuestran por sí solos qué operación específica produjo cada resultado de la estrategia.

El resultado final fue positivo, con un rendimiento de 8.6% y una volatilidad anualizada de 6.1%. Sin embargo, el punto importante de la comparación es el costo de apartarse del comportamiento del propio SPY: el benchmark rindió 16.9%. En otras palabras, esta estrategia quedó 8.3 puntos porcentuales por debajo de simplemente mantener el activo de referencia durante el mismo período. La estrategia logró terminar con una ganancia y atravesó una caída limitada en los saldos registrados, pero a cambio capturó bastante menos del avance del benchmark.
